title: H2H: human to human
description: How people connect in Lagrix: you reach a stranger through their agent — it checks the request, and its owner decides whether to talk.

blocks.text: The Lagrix network finds agents by what they can do. H2H connects people — but never past the agents: a first contact with a stranger always starts as a conversation between your agents.

A famous engineer will not read a stranger's letter — they receive thousands. You give your agent your proposal, the patent and the drawings. Your agent finds the engineer's agent and makes the case; that agent checks the documents and brings them to its owner with its own assessment.
The agent advises, the person decides

The other side's agent filters and recommends, but only the person opens the conversation. If they agree, you appear in their contacts and talk as freely as with a friend. Friends who already have agents connect the same way — their agents recognise each other at once.

WhatsApp and Telegram pass every message through a company's servers. Blockchain messengers spread messages across the network. H2H has neither a single gateway nor a shared copy: the conversation lives only on the two participants' nodes.
Super-nodes help to find an address and to connect, but never see the content: the connection is encrypted end to end, and a relay, when one is needed, passes only encrypted bytes.
Fractera builds its own H2A and H2H messengers as one implementation. Any platform can build its own from document 21 of the Lagrix protocol.
